meetings.headline: Board will push legal action against Woodlands condo trust over kayak racks in the well's protected zone
meetings.summary: The Lunenburg Water District Commissioners reviewed the in-house cost of the Roland Acres water main replacement versus hiring it out, discussed a near-final draft of a community engagement survey on water source options, and spent significant time on the Woodlands condo trust's refusal to remove kayak racks from the well's Zone One protection area, concluding they will pursue legal action if the racks are not voluntarily moved. The meeting also covered SRF grant funding status, a possible new hire and equipment purchase for future in-house projects, a proposal to explore alternative voting methods for ratepayers, and recognized the superintendent's 40th work anniversary, closing with extended public comment challenging the survey's cost estimates.

budget_items.what_was_said: Commissioners discussed bringing on another employee in late winter/early spring to continue in-house main replacement work, and agreed to start putting together the annual expense estimate for staffing and equipment to present at a future meeting.

budget_items.topic: O&M cost differential between water source options (survey)
budget_items.what_was_said: A resident presented his own analysis arguing the operations-and-maintenance cost difference between two water-source combination options was understated in the district's consultant figures, using a baseline and a variable-cost percentage split; the district said its consultants (Tighe & Bond) were confident in their numbers but did not have them itemized as a line item.

budget_items.what_was_said: A resident questioned why moving from a two-source to a three-source treatment configuration added several million dollars in capital cost; the superintendent explained it required a larger treatment plant and a raw water transmission main.

decisions.decision: Staff will begin putting together annual expense projections for hiring an additional employee and for equipment, to bring to a future meeting as part of a three-to-five-year plan.
The community engagement survey draft will be finalized and brought back to the board for approval before release, alongside a draft postcard mailer and website.

The district will continue pursuing removal of the Woodlands condo trust's kayak racks from the Zone One well protection area, through its attorney if necessary, and will seek to recover costs from the Woodlands if legal action becomes necessary.

The clerk/president will look into whether the district's bylaws allow shutting off a ratepayer for non-compliance with district regulations (not just non-payment), and report back at the next meeting.
The board will ask town counsel whether an alternative voting method (e.g., a paper ballot period before the meeting) could legally be offered to increase ratepayer participation.

public_comment.topic: Resident asked the auditor whether expense categories are the same year to year and whether deviations could be missed, then asked about the rise in accounts receivable and about county retirement returns.
Resident questioned a water bill that jumped from about 1100 to 5900 cubic feet, asked whether meters can be wrong, and asked for an adjustment and a payment arrangement.
Resident asked whether changing the meter would help; staff explained testing and calibration.

votes.motion: Motion to adjourn, moved and apparently seconded; captions cut off.

budget_items.what_was_said: The auditor said the district received an unmodified opinion on the June 30, 2024 financials.
Cash rose at year end and short-term borrowing for the water main project rose by a similar amount; the district earned interest on the cash.
Water revenue rose, attributed mainly to the new rate system, even though fewer gallons were pumped.
Receivables rose, which the auditor called unsurprising given larger bills.
Wage lines rose slightly more than the budgeted base-salary increase because of on-call, emergency and overtime pay.
Reported pension expense is an actuarial amount and differs from the required cash contribution.
Operating expense rose, driven mostly by pilot studies; supplies and corrosion control were up.
A board member said the cost of a system-wide meter replacement would be weighed against added revenue from more accurate readings.
The RFP drew no bids; the board will rebid and may add the Sunny Hill Road tank.
Replacement wells would yield less than the original well, making a large spend poor value.
The district keeps being billed a betterment for a sewer line it says does not pass its property, and the board debated paying it off.
The bill will be recomputed at the first-tier rate after a leak stopped, with payment options to be discussed.

decisions.decision: The board will charge the resident's high usage at the flat tier one rate and staff will recalculate the bill the next day.
Staff will redo the cellular equipment RFP, possibly adding the Sunny Hill Road tank.
The board deferred a decision on paying off the sewer betterment and will research it further.
The engineers will come to the next meeting on the 22nd to present the final pilot testing report.

what_happened.line: The auditor reported an unmodified opinion on the district's June 30, 2024 financial statements and walked commissioners through the main variances.
The board agreed to charge a resident's leak-inflated usage at the flat first-tier rate, with staff to recalculate the bill the next day.
The cellular equipment RFP drew no bids; staff will redo it, possibly adding the Sunny Hill Road tank.
The board deferred a decision on paying off a sewer betterment it says does not apply to district property, and will research it further.
The engineers are due at the next meeting, on the 22nd, to present the final pilot testing report.

why_it_matters: The audit result and the stated rise in operating expense from pilot studies bear on the water rates and revenue residents pay under the new rate system.
The leak-bill decision shows how the district handles a bill inflated by a leak, which matters to any customer who finds a sudden jump in usage.
The sewer betterment and the unbid cell-tower lease are open items that could add a cost or leave revenue uncollected until the board resolves them.
